mechanism: Fit CLinearCDF (ECDF with linear spline between sample points) on each margin of a bivariate price/return matrix; to_quantile maps raw levels to (0,1) uniforms via the Probability Integral Transform, clipping away exact 0/1. Copula is then fit on these pseudo-observations so dependence is separated from marginal shape.
data_needed: Paired close (or log-return) series; optional upper/lower quantile bounds (default 1e-5..1-1e-5).
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: NZDUSD vs AUDUSD D1 ECDF_Demo (HistoryLength=1000 from 2024-01-01); XAUEUR D1 sampling tests; general bivariate FX/metals
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a reusable PIT/ECDF front-end so any downstream dependence or tail sensor runs on rank-uniform space rather than raw prices—required for regime-stable cross-asset sensing.
quote: By transforming marginals to uniform distributions, we can analyze how variables are linked without the influence of their individual distributions.

mechanism: Bivariate Gaussian copula (ρ from covariance) is radially symmetric with weak/zero asymptotic tail dependence. Student's t-copula adds ν (degrees of freedom): lower ν ⇒ stronger joint extremes in both tails; as ν→∞ it converges to Gaussian. Fit via Kendall τ→ρ and optional ν MLE; Conditional_Probability and Copula_PDF expose joint-extreme likelihood.
data_needed: Uniform margins (u,v); 2×2 covariance or Kendall τ; ν for t-copula.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Synthetic samples on XAUEUR D1; library validated vs ArbitrageLab unit tests; financial returns cited as use case
why_new_for_mis: MIS can sense crash/boom co-movement regimes that linear correlation and Gaussian copulas miss—ν and λ_tail become explicit joint-volatility features.
quote: Unlike the Gaussian copula, the t-copula exhibits non-zero tail dependence, meaning that extreme events in one variable make extremes in the other more likely.

mechanism: Map pair dependence to Archimedean families by tail signature: Clayton (λ_L=2^{-1/θ}, λ_U=0) for joint downturns; Gumbel/Joe (upper-tail λ_U only) for joint rallies; Frank (radial symmetry, no tails) for mid-distribution concordance; N14 both tails (asymmetric), N13 mid-range without asymptotic tails. θ from Kendall τ (closed form or Brent). AIC/BIC/HQIC pick best family on PIT data.
data_needed: Pseudo-observations from ECDF; candidate copula set; log-likelihood → AIC/BIC/HQIC.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: XAUUSD–XAUEUR selection on ~260 D1 bars from 2025-01-01 (Frank best in demo); Concordance universe AUDUSD,NZDUSD,XAUUSD,XAGUSD,EURUSD,XAUEUR
why_new_for_mis: Family identity itself is a dependence-regime label (lower-tail / upper-tail / center-only)—MIS can track which tail structure currently fits a pair without assuming symmetry.
quote: The Clayton copula exhibits lower-tail dependence... making it particularly suitable for modeling situations where extreme low values tend to occur together.

mechanism: After fitting copula+ECDF, map live closes to quantiles (u1,u2). Signals from crossed conditional CDFs: if C(u1|u2)≤0.05 and C(u2|u1)≥0.95 treat symbol1 undervalued / symbol2 overvalued (and the reverse at 0.95/0.05). Exits when conditionals cross upper/lower thresholds (AND or OR rule). GoldCopulaSignals plots both conditionals with levels at 0.05/0.5/0.95.
data_needed: Saved ECDF+copula models; live closes for both symbols; open/exit probability thresholds.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: XAUUSD vs XAUEUR (in-sample EA SimpleCopulaPairsStrategy); chart period of indicator; session window 06:00–23:55
why_new_for_mis: Converts fitted dependence into a continuous dual conditional-probability state for relative mispricing—quantile-based change sensor beyond z-score spreads.
quote: If C(u_1 | u_2) <= 0.05 and C(u_2 | u_1) >= 0.95, then Symbol 1 is considered undervalued and Symbol 2 is over-valued

mechanism: Concordance.mq5 builds a dependence matrix over a symbol universe using Kendall τ or Spearman ρ on raw closes or log-returns; selects the pair with maximum off-diagonal concordance as the strongest co-movement candidate for copula modeling.
data_needed: Multi-symbol close matrix; ENUM_DEPENDENCE_MEASURE; bar count and timeframe; Use_Returns flag.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: AUDUSD,NZDUSD,XAUUSD,XAGUSD,EURUSD,XAUEUR; D1; 260 bars from 2025-01-01 (XAUUSD–XAUEUR top in demo)
why_new_for_mis: Rank-based concordance screen is a portable co-movement regime filter MIS can run before heavier dependence models.
quote: High concordance points to strong co-movement. Pairs with the highest values for Kendall's tau or Spearman's rho are selected.

mechanism: Linear mixture C=Σ w_i C_i with Σw_i=1. CFG (Clayton–Frank–Gumbel) and CTG (Clayton–Student-t–Gumbel) combine lower-tail, center/symmetric-tail, and upper-tail components. EM (+ optional SCAD penalty on weights via 5-fold CV on λ,a) estimates w and θ; large w on Clayton vs Gumbel vs Frank/t reads as crash-co-move vs rally-co-move vs mid-dependence regime. Mixture Conditional_Probability drives the same pairs mispricing indicator/EA path.
data_needed: PIT matrix; SCAD gamma/a (or MLE); max EM iters; mixture enum CFG/CTG/CFJ/JFG.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: XAUUSD–XAUEUR D1, HistorySize=1200 from 2025-01-01; Scad_CV + MixedCopulaSelection; GoldMixedCopulaSignals EA path
why_new_for_mis: Mixture weights are an interpretable multi-tail dependence-regime vector—closer to regime-switching dependence than any single copula parameter.
quote: These combinations are designed to capture both asymmetric tail dependence and potential regime-switching behavior within the data.

mechanism: Library tutorial for CHttpBody (AddString/AddJson/AddBinary, UTF-8 char arrays, Content-Type headers) wrapping WebRequest POST bodies; httpbin echo tests. No market feature is constructed.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: n/a (httpbin.org POST examples; EURUSD fields only as sample JSON payload)
why_new_for_mis: No market sensing idea after full read—HTTP client body plumbing for Connexus only.
quote: In this article, we explored the concept of body in HTTP requests, showing its fundamental role in data transmission between client and server.

mechanism: SYMBOL_TRADE_STOPS_LEVEL==0 is treated as FLOATING: broker derives live min SL/TP from spread (tool annotates ~2–3× current SYMBOL_SPREAD points). Non-zero levels are fixed-point floors. Panel refreshes on a 2s timer because stops/spread can widen in news or thin liquidity—turning stops distance into a live liquidity/friction sensor.
data_needed: SymbolInfoInteger STOPS_LEVEL, SPREAD, SPREAD_FLOAT; SYMBOL_POINT for price conversion.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: XAUUSD rulebook comparison Broker A (floating 0) vs Broker B (70 pts fixed); any Market Watch symbol; chart attach + optional CSV sweep
why_new_for_mis: Exposes zero-stops as a dynamic spread-multiple constraint MIS can track as a per-symbol liquidity friction regime, not a static contract constant.
quote: IMPORTANT: 0 does NOT mean "no limit". It means the level is FLOATING - the broker derives the real minimum live from the spread (commonly 2-3x it), so it changes tick by tick

mechanism: AuditSymbol grades SYMBOL_TRADE_MODE (non-FULL=breaker), FILLING_MODE bitmask (FOK/IOC/Return), FREEZE_LEVEL, VOLUME_MIN/STEP, ORDER_MODE market bit, swap+triple-swap day, and floating/fixed spread into OK/WARN/BAD; Market Watch CSV dump compares brokers. Amber flags are code-fit warnings; red is symbol refuses free trading.
data_needed: SymbolInfoInteger/Double for trade mode, filling, freeze, volumes, order mode, swap, spread; optional InpAuditAll/CSV.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Live chart panel; XAUUSD Broker A vs B table; full Market Watch sweep to BrokerAudit.csv
why_new_for_mis: Packages broker microstructure (fill policy, freeze zone, lot step, trade mode) as graded sensors MIS can use to gate signals by venue tradability and liquidity frictions.
quote: I once shipped a gold scalper that ran fine for me. A client mounted it on a broker whose XAUUSD had a stops level of 70 points and only allowed IOC filling.
